mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the permission matrix fact allows the model to invent arbitrary permission assignments, violating the least-privilege principle that admin operations must be a superset of member operations.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionViolation { Member -> OpEditTask in PermMatrix.allowed and Admin -> OpDeleteTask not in PermMatrix.allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the audit-immutability constraint allows the model to create audit entries with inconsistent field counts, violating the append-only and completeness invariants.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMutation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.id = ae2.id and ae1.actor != ae2.actor }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing assignee validation allows the model to assign a task to a user from a different team, violating the requirement that assignees must be members of the task's team.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AssigneeTeamViolation { some t: Task, u: User | t.assignee = u and (no m: TeamMembership | m.user = u and m.team = t.team) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the unique-role-per-user-team constraint allows a user to have multiple roles in the same team, violating the per-team-role invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MultipleRoles { some u: User, t: Team, disj r1, r2: Role | some m1, m2: TeamMembership | m1.user = u and m1.team = t and m1.role = r1 and m2.user = u and m2.team = t and m2.role = r2 }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the structural isolation constraint allows a single task to belong to multiple teams, violating the requirement that tasks are isolated by team.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TaskMultiTeam { some t: Task, disj team1, team2: Team | t.team = team1 and t.team = team2 }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing owner-immutability allows a task's owner to change, violating the immutability requirement.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnerChange { some t: Task, disj u1, u2: User | t.owner = u1 and t.owner = u2 }
